text: A deterministic rule costs microseconds and basically nothing. An LLM call costs real tokens and real wall-clock time — fine for a one-off, and a real problem inside a loop.
A per-row LLM call looks fine with 50 demo rows. At a million rows a day, even a fraction of a cent and a few hundred milliseconds per call adds up to real dollars and a latency bottleneck.
Most of what looks like an LLM's job inside a pipeline is actually a lookup table or a regex — those win on cost, latency, and predictability when the logic is enumerable.
A one-time batch job or offline pass pays the token cost once, outside the live latency budget — that's where the call belongs, not whether you ever use one.
Cheap and fast where a rule applies; the LLM reserved for genuinely ambiguous, low-volume, or offline work. Next up: evaluating AI output for correctness.
